subject: Cerberus commit sizing: throughput baseline & headroom
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@cerberus-systems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cerberus commit sizing: throughput baseline & headroom

Alex — thank you again for the call this morning. As promised, attaching our preliminary commit sizing that ties your projected monthly token commit to expected TPS and p95 latency headroom. High-level summary below; full numbers in the attached spreadsheet.

Baseline assumptions
- Model: open-llm-3-large (quantized int8 recommended for cost/latency trade).
- Average response length: 90 tokens; 80% short (<120 tokens), 20% long (>400 tokens) per current usage pattern.
- Concurrency pattern: steady daytime traffic with 3x hourly spikes for short bursts.

Preliminary throughput mapping
- Committed monthly tokens: 1.2B tokens/mo (as you indicated).
- Sustained tokens/sec (avg): 450 tps across the day (workload-shaped).
- Peak observed spikes: instantaneous bursts up to ~1,700 tps for short windows (10–60s).

SLO fit and headroom
- Target SLO: 95% requests under 180ms p95 for inference (in-region).
- Recommended dedicated slab: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed 80/20 quantized run) -> baseline supports ~1,000 sustained tps with 30% headroom for bursts and KV-cache warmup.
- If you need hard 99th guarantees under 250ms, we recommend a burst slab (2 extra GPUs) or routing fallback to a lower-cost variant during extreme spikes.

Risks / open items
- Cold KV-cache for long-context flows can add ~40–80ms for first few tokens; we'll instrument cache warmup windows.
- Long-tail ( >1k tokens) requests affect per-token mix — need sample traces for accurate p99 costing.

Ask
1) Can you confirm the monthly commit and percent of long responses?
2) Are you able to share a small sample of request size distribution (anonymized) so we can finalize p99 risk sizing?
3) Can we schedule a 30-min ops-runthrough with your infra lead this week?

I attached the spreadsheet (cerberus_commit_model_v1.xlsx) with the line-level math and recommended slab SKUs. Ben — I looped you for the ops/engineering sizing and fallback plan.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cerberus commit sizing: throughput baseline & headroom

Thanks, Neha — this is a helpful start. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed committed monthly tokens: 1.2B.
- Long responses: roughly 12% of calls exceed 400 tokens (not 20% as you modeled) — this should help reduce p99 tail cost.
- SLO question: p95 < 180ms is our ideal, but we actually need to keep user-facing chat p99 under 300ms during business hours. If that requires an explicit burst slab, we can discuss budget trade-offs.

We can provide anonymized request-size histogram (hourly snapshots) — I'll have Jordan pull that and share by EOD.

One more ask: during spikes we have a user-critical flow that cannot fall back to a smaller model; if you recommend fallback we need a documented failover that preserves business logic and logs the downgrade.

Happy to hop on a call Thursday 11am PT with Ben to walk through the slab numbers.

—Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Platform Engineering | Cerberus Systems
alex.torres@cerberus-systems.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@cerberus-systems.com>
Date: 2027-04-08T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cerberus commit sizing: throughput baseline & headroom

Alex / Neha — quick engineering-run numbers after looking at the sheet and running a quick sim:

Engine assumptions
- A100-equivalent GPU (fp16) baseline: ~125 tps for mixed short/medium responses (90 token avg) at p95 ~160–180ms when KV cache warm.
- Quantized int8 path improves cost by ~25% and gives ~10–15% better steady-state tps for short responses; tail benefits limited.

Recommended slab plan (optimize for p95 and p99 during bursts):
- Prod slab: 6 x A100-equivalent for steady-state -> handles ~750 sustained tps with 20% safety margin.
- Burst slab: +2 GPUs (hot standby) that auto-attaches on spike detection -> headroom to ~1,100–1,200 tps for 60–120s windows.
- Extra buffer: reserve one smaller instance for the non-failable critical flow you mentioned (keeps a copy of model on a pinned GPU with strict CPU/GPU affinity).

Latency notes
- With slab above and proactive KV-cache warmup (prefetch first 5 tokens on session start), p95 should be <180ms most windows and p99 <300ms with burst slab attached.
- If Cerberus requires contractual 99% under 300ms during business hours, we should size the burst policy conservatively (attach at 60% of predicted spike) and include surge-credit terms in the contract.

Ops playbook (short)
- Spike detection: rolling 30s EMA on request rate -> trigger burst attach at >60% of slab capacity.
- Fallback: route to quantized variant only for long-tail >800 tokens; log the event and tag in observability so we can alert you.

I'll export the resilience-slab-mapping.pdf with the graph overlays and attach to this thread.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: resilience-slab-mapping.pdf (pdf)

Alex — brilliant, thanks for confirming the long-response mix. Jordan — appreciate the histogram when you have it.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Jordan to share anonymized request-size histograms by EOD 2027-04-08 (helps finalize p99 math).
2) Redwood to finalize slab sizing + SLA language and post a Draft SOW + surge-credit clause by 2027-04-12. (Ben will populate the ops playbook section.)
3) We’ll provision a short performance run (3 days) on the recommended slab once the SOW is signed to validate p95/p99 under traffic replays.
4) DocuSign: I will send the initial SOW link after internal sign-off — attaching the reference DocuSign link here: https://docusign.com/cerberus/CERB-commit-0427

If those steps look good I’ll lock Thursday 11am PT for the product/ops call.

Thanks again — reaching alignment on burst policy and the reserved copy for the critical flow will keep your business logic safe while optimizing cost.

Best,
